name: concurrent-links
description: One initiator opens link_count links to a single responder and holds them all open at once, keeping exactly one send in flight on every link (refilling the link that just settled) for the wall-time, then closes them all. Where establishment-churn pays one full handshake per cycle serially, this measures breadth: how many simultaneous links a transport node carries in its link table while every one of them stays live. The host relays each as a transported link, so the count it sustains is the table's business, not a storage constant - the scenario a fixed 1024 cap or an O(n) table lookup would have throttled.
conformance: Every one of link_count links establishes - proof the host's transported-link table held them all - and delivers at least once over the wall-time, proof the host kept switching each; sent == delivered + timeouts. A capped host fails at establishment past its ceiling; a host that drops a carried link leaves that link silent and trips the per-link delivery check. A Prns pair settles zero timeouts. Known reference asymmetry: a reference initiator opening all 256 links at once hits its own per-packet receipt deadlines under that concurrency and settles a few hundred timeouts - conformant by the identity (every link still delivers, so no link went dark), and the contrast is the point: Prns carries 256 live links with zero drops. link_count is held modest (256) so a Python reference client, which opens each link with a full handshake, stays tractable.
